f: Lagging metrics are the financial results of a business, specifically profit and revenue, which are at least six-month lagging indicators. These numbers appear on the balance sheet after business decisions have already been implemented and their effects have had time to materialize. Leading indicators, by contrast, are the specific actions and measurable activities that predict future results. For example, in media buying on Meta, leading indicators include the number of new ad concepts created, AI videos produced, static images created, and winning ads identified. If these leading indicators show positive results, a business owner can confidently predict positive profitability outcomes approximately one month ahead.

The critical difference lies in timing and control. While lagging metrics only reveal what has already happened, leading indicators allow managers to identify problems and make corrections before financial damage occurs. By tracking leading actions weekly, business leaders can spot disconnects between their activities and financial results, then adjust their strategies accordingly. When leading indicators are all green but lagging metrics show negative numbers, it signals a fundamental problem in how those leading actions were identified, requiring a complete reassessment of which activities actually drive desired business outcomes.

88d8d1e989.q: Why did Thrasio go bankrupt and what role did inventory play in the collapse?
88d8d1e989.a: Thrasio went bankrupt not only due to poor execution but primarily because they massively overpurchased inventory. They ended up with five to ten years worth of inventory and even twenty years worth of inventory on certain SKUs because they did not have good processes, checks and balances, or the right operating system in place. This demonstrates why inventory is described as the kryptonite for e-commerce brands and how poor inventory management is where the best brands go to die.
